note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure.
  - 5-day history of dry cough and constant nasal discharge. No specific trigger or exposure identified.
- Symptom timeline and progression.
  - Onset ~5 days ago. Dry cough occurring every 20–30 minutes. Nasal discharge persistent.
- ENT symptoms (as applicable): throat swelling/closure sensation, voice change, dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling, nasal/ocular symptoms, stridor/noisy breathing, dyspnea, distribution of swelling (lips/tongue/uvula/face), ear/neck symptoms.
  - Nasal: constant streaming; patient reports discharge “pretty green.” No epistaxis.
  - Throat: not clearly reported; patient notes Lemsip “soothes my throat” at night (symptom severity not detailed).
  - Ears: not reported.
  - Breathing: no dyspnea, no chest pain, no hemoptysis. No noisy breathing/stridor reported.
  - Voice change, dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling, facial/oral swelling: not reported.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments (including any prior hospital care or injection therapy).
  - No prior similar infections requiring treatment reported. No ED/hospital care mentioned.
- Allergies and current medications (mark missing dose/route/frequency as not documented).
  - Allergies: seasonal allergic rhinitis (hay fever) reported; no known drug allergies.
  - Medications:
    - Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented).
    - Lisinopril: patient reports “200” (unit not specified; dose unclear).
    - Lemsip (paracetamol-containing OTC cold remedy) 2–3 doses/day.
    - No home blood glucose monitoring equipment; does not check sugars.
- Any relevant social context (e.g., accompaniment/supervision).
  - Lives with partner and a dog. Works as an office manager. Alcohol: occasional (“odd cherry”). Smoking status not recorded.

Objective:
- Observable swelling and distribution (e.g., lips, tongue, uvula, face) if stated.
  - Not reported.
- Airway/breathing descriptors if stated (e.g., stridor, work of breathing).
  - No shortness of breath; no reports of noisy breathing/stridor.
- Mental status and associated features (e.g., dizziness, syncope) if stated.
  - Reports feeling hot and occasionally chills; no dizziness/syncope reported.
- Vitals and examination findings only if mentioned; otherwise note “Not recorded.”
  - Not recorded. No thermometer measurement taken.
- Presence of another person with the patient (if stated).
  - Not stated.

Assessment:
- Likely viral upper respiratory tract infection with rhinitis and dry cough.
  - Justification: 5-day course; dry cough; persistent nasal discharge (green noted by patient); systemic symptoms (feeling hot/chills); no dyspnea, no chest pain, no hemoptysis; normal oral intake and hydration.
  - Risk factor: Diabetes mellitus increases risk of secondary bacterial infection.
  - Medication detail issue: patient-reported lisinopril dose “200” unclear (conflict noted).

Plan:
- Immediate actions taken/advised:
  - Supportive care. Continue Lemsip as needed but avoid any additional paracetamol-containing products concurrently.
  - Cough syrup: not advised during daytime; acceptable in small amount at night if cough disrupts sleep.
  - Obtain a thermometer and monitor temperature.
- Specific instructions provided to patient/caregiver:
  - Check temperature regularly.
  - Maintain hydration and usual diet as tolerated.
  - Ensure routine diabetes and blood pressure check-ups with primary care.
- Escalation criteria/red flags:
  - Seek further medical advice if:
    - Persistent or rising fever (>37.5–38°C) or ongoing temperature spikes.
    - Worsening cough, development of copious “nasty” phlegm, hemoptysis, or nosebleeds.
    - New shortness of breath or chest pain.
- Follow-up:
  - If symptoms persist or worsen, re-evaluation for possible bacterial infection and consideration of antibiotics.
  - No ENT or allergy referral discussed.
- COVID-19 vaccine suitability:
  - Not discussed.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Objective ENT exam (oropharynx, nasal cavity, ears), vitals including temperature, oxygen saturation.
  - Smoking status.
  - Detailed throat symptoms (sore throat severity, dysphagia/odynophagia), ear pain, voice change.
  - Precise medication doses/routes/frequencies for metformin and lisinopril.
  - Home blood glucose monitoring plan not established.
- Internal conflicts:
  - Lisinopril dose reported as “200” with no unit specified; dose likely inaccurate (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality:
  - Some sections inaudible/unclear (address incomplete; minor gaps). Overall history adequate for preliminary assessment.
